newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil - barges up, but cargoes steady.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil - barges up, but cargoes steady.

text.p: The NWE fuel oil market saw firmer barges, but steady to weaker caroges on Monday.
Dealers said barges traded as high as $124 fob ARA a tonne early but later fell back to $120-122.
"We had a little rush up on crude, but that's slipped back and there are no buyers anymore," said one barge broker.
The high sulphur cargo market was steady to a touch firmer around $115-116 cif NWE.
"There is a feeling stuff will get done this week ahead of Christmas," said one trader at a major, who thought end-users would come out of the woodwork.
The low sulphur market looked long. A 25,000 tonne cargo with early January loading dates was heard offered around $127 fob NWE.
"Its gone a bit quiet as the market digests the gain and then subsequent loss of crude," said one dealer.
Low sulphur straight run has been given a filip by crude on the price side, but activity was still very slack.
"There's no decent buying and no U.S interest," said a supplier.
